verdict.rationale: Blaxel documents API keys (long-lived) and short-lived OAuth tokens usable across its API, CLI and SDK. It also issues time-limited, scoped session tokens for operating sandboxes, which is its own least-privilege credential mechanism, though it is framed for frontend clients rather than agents. Nothing shows that API keys themselves can be restricted by permission, role or resource, or issued per agent. missing for 10: documented per-key permission/role scoping, agent-specific credential issuance, granular scope definitions beyond sandbox sessions, independent corroboration.
